explanation:
The meeting was extended by 30 minutes because no conclusion was reached. / We will extend the opening hours until 7:00.

---

- **延長する（えんちょう）** — to extend, prolong (period of time, deadline, etc.); transitive verb. From 延(の)びる "to stretch" + 長(なが)い "long". [JLPT N2]
- **〜される** — passive form; in the first sentence, 会議は延長された is a direct passive (the meeting is extended by someone/something). [JLPT N5]
- **結論が出ない** — set phrase meaning "to reach a conclusion" (literally: a conclusion does not emerge). 結論は出る is an intransitive collocation. [JLPT N3]

In winter, the zoo's operating hours are shortened. / To shorten {time/distance ...}.

---

- **短縮する（たんしゅく）** — to shorten, reduce (length, time, distance); transitive verb. Contrast: 延長する (to extend). [JLPT N2]
- **営業時間が短縮される** — passive construction; 営業時間 is the subject undergoing the action. [JLPT N5]

In this area, the reception is poor and the TV picture keeps breaking up.

---

- **映像（えいぞう）** — image, picture, video (on a screen); noun. Distinguish from 画像(がぞう) which refers more to still images/photos. [JLPT N2]
- **電波の状態が悪い** — "reception is poor" (literally: the condition of radio waves is bad). Common collocation for TV/phone signal issues. [JLPT N3]
- **乱れる（みだれる）** — to become disturbed, disrupted, thrown into disorder; intransitive verb. Here it describes the image breaking up/glitching. [JLPT N3]

I had a professional photographer take my portrait. / They were filming a movie in front of the station.

---

- **撮影する（さつえい）** — to photograph, film, shoot (video or photos); transitive verb. [JLPT N2]
- **〜てもらう** — benefactive construction indicating the speaker received the favor of someone doing something. プロのカメラマンに撮影してもらった = "I had a professional photographer take (my photo)." [JLPT N4]
- Note: 撮影 can refer to both still photography and video/film shooting. The verb 撮る alone is more casual and usually for photos.

This is a family photo, and the background is our garden. / The background of a {painting/screen/stage ...}.

---

- **背景（はいけい）** — background (in a photo, painting, stage setting, etc.); noun. Also used figuratively for the circumstances or reasons behind something (e.g., 事件の背景 "the background of the incident"). [JLPT N2]
- **〜で** — particle indicating location/context in the first sentence; in the pattern frame, の marks possession/attribution. [JLPT N5]

America gained independence from Britain.

---

- **独立する（どくりつ）** — to become independent, gain independence; intransitive verb. Literally "to stand on one's own." Can refer to political independence or personal/financial independence (親から独立する). [JLPT N2]
- **〜から独立する** — to become independent from (a country, parent, organization). [JLPT N2]

The upcoming mayoral election will be contested by five candidates. / Tokyo has become a candidate city for hosting the Olympics.

---

- **候補（こうほ）** — candidate, prospect; noun. A person or thing under consideration for selection. Often appears as 候補者(こうほしゃ) when referring specifically to people. [JLPT N2]
- **〜で争われる** — passive of 争う(あらそう) "to compete, contest"; the election is fought/contested by five candidates. [JLPT N3]
- **開催地（かいさいち）** — host location, venue (for an event). [JLPT N2]

I support the prime minister. / Takahashi's opinion gained wide support.

---

- **支持する（しじ）** — to support, back (a person, policy, opinion); transitive verb. Used for political support, supporting opinions/theories. Not used for physically supporting objects. Contrast: 支援(しえん) which emphasizes material/financial aid. [JLPT N2]
- **支持を得る** — set phrase: "to gain support." [JLPT N3]

I voted for candidate A in the election.

---

- **投票する（とうひょう）** — to vote, cast a ballot; can be transitive or intransitive. Takes に to indicate the candidate voted for. [JLPT N2]
- **A候補に投票する** — note the particle に marks the recipient/target of the vote, not を. [JLPT N2]

In the recent election, someone I know was elected mayor.

---

- **当選する（とうせん）** — to win an election, be elected; intransitive verb. Only used for elections, lotteries, and similar competitive selections. Contrast: 落選(らくせん) "to lose an election." [JLPT N2]
- **市長に当選する** — note the particle に indicates the position won. [JLPT N2]

I won the lottery and got a TV.

---

- **抽選（ちゅうせん）** — lottery, drawing; noun. A method of selection by random draw. 抽選に当たる means "to win the lottery." [JLPT N2]
- **抽選に当たる（あたる）** — to win a lottery/drawing. 当たる here means "to hit" (the winning number). [JLPT N3]
- Note: 抽選する as a verb is less common; more often used as a noun (抽選で決める "decide by lottery").

We distribute flyers to pedestrians in front of the station.

---

- **配布する/配付する（はいふ）** — to distribute, hand out (documents, flyers, materials); transitive verb. Both 配布 and 配付 are used; 配布 is more common in modern usage. [JLPT N2]
- **ちらし** — flyer, handbill. A wago term; the kanji equivalent would be ビラ (also a loanword). [JLPT N3]

If you commit a serious foul in a match, you get disqualified.

---

- **失格する（しっかく）** — to be disqualified, lose eligibility; intransitive verb. Used in sports, competitions, exams. Contrast: 合格(ごうかく) "to pass (an exam)." [JLPT N2]
- **反則（はんそく）** — foul, violation (of rules). [JLPT N2]
- **〜になる** — indicates a change of state: becomes disqualified. [JLPT N5]

I do volunteer work in my spare time.

---

- **余暇（よか）** — spare time, leisure time; noun. A somewhat formal/literary term; in everyday speech, 暇(ひま) or 自由時間(じゆうじかん) is more common. [JLPT N2]
- **〜を利用して** — "making use of..." 利用する(りようする) "to utilize, make use of." Slightly more formal than 使う. [JLPT N3]

New Year's events/customs vary by region.

---

- **行事（ぎょうじ）** — event, function, ceremony, annual activity; noun. Refers to organized events, especially traditional/seasonal ones (学校の行事, 年中行事). Not used for casual personal activities. [JLPT N2]
- **正月（しょうがつ）** — New Year (period). [JLPT N4]
- **地方（ちほう）** — region, area, locality. Also means "the provinces, rural areas" (as opposed to Tokyo). [JLPT N3]
- **さまざまだ** — various, diverse. The na-adjective 様々(さまざま) + だ. [JLPT N3]

I would like young people to have high ideals.

---

- **理想（りそう）** — ideal; noun. Shared with Chinese (理想 lǐxiǎng), same meaning. [JLPT N2]
- **〜を持ってもらう** — causative-benefactive: "to have someone possess/hold..." 持つ here is used figuratively (to hold ideals). [JLPT N4]

Ideals and reality are different.

---

- **現実（げんじつ）** — reality, actuality; noun. Shared with Chinese (现实 xiànshí), same meaning. Contrast with 理想. [JLPT N2]
- **違う（ちがう）** — to differ, be different; intransitive verb. Also means "to be wrong/mistaken" in other contexts. [JLPT N4]

In Japan, the generation that has never experienced war is growing.

---

- **体験する（たいけん）** — to experience (firsthand), go through; transitive verb. Emphasizes personal, direct experience rather than learning about something indirectly. Contrast: 経験(けいけん) which is broader and includes accumulated experience over time. [JLPT N2]
- **〜ことのない世代** — "a generation that has never..." のない is a literary/negative attributive modifier. [JLPT N3]
- **増えている** — is increasing (progressive form of 増える). The intransitive verb 増える(ふえる) indicates natural growth. [JLPT N4]

My younger brother does nothing but daydream and refuses to face reality.

---

- **空想する（くうそう）** — to daydream, fantasize, imagine; intransitive/transitive verb. Imagination divorced from reality. Contrast: 想像(そうぞう) which is more neutral ("to imagine"). [JLPT N2]
- **〜ばかりして** — "doing nothing but..." ばかり indicates exclusivity, often with a negative nuance. [JLPT N4]
- **〜ようとしない** — "makes no attempt to..." / "refuses to..." Volitional form + としない expresses refusal or lack of intention to do something. [JLPT N3]

This diamond looks big in the photo, but the actual item is even smaller.

---

- **実物（じつぶつ）** — the actual object, the real thing; noun. Used to contrast with a photo, replica, or description. Contrast: 本物(ほんもの) which contrasts with 偽物(にせもの) (fake). [JLPT N2]
- **〜に見える** — "looks..." / "appears to be..." に marks the state of appearance. [JLPT N4]
- **もっと** — even more, still more. Used here for comparison: the real thing is smaller still. [JLPT N5]

I realized a long-cherished dream. / A long-held dream came true.

---

- **実現する（じつげん）** — to realize, make come true, bring into reality; transitive/intransitive verb. Can be used transitively (夢を実現する) or intransitively (夢が実現する). Shared with Chinese (实现 shíxiàn). [JLPT N2]
- **長年の夢（ながねんのゆめ）** — a dream/ambition held for many years. [JLPT N2]
- **{を/が}** — either particle works: 夢を実現した (transitive: I realized my dream) or 夢が実現した (intransitive: my dream came true).

The event was carried out as scheduled.

---

- **実施する（じっし）** — to carry out, implement, conduct (a plan, policy, event, measure); transitive verb. Used for official/formal actions: 調査を実施する, 政策を実施する. [JLPT N2]
- **予定どおり** — as planned, as scheduled. 通り(どおり) "according to." [JLPT N3]
- **〜された** — passive form: the event was carried out (by the organizers). [JLPT N5]

You need police permission to take photos on the street.

---

- **許可する（きょか）** — to permit, authorize, give permission; transitive verb. Official/formal permission, usually from an authority. Contrast: 許す is broader and more personal (to forgive, allow). [JLPT N2]
- **路上での撮影** — photography on the street. 路上(ろじょう) "on the road, on the street." の makes the noun phrase modify 撮影. [JLPT N2]
- **〜には〜が必要だ** — "for X, Y is necessary." Standard necessity construction. [JLPT N4]

This company has a total of about 500 employees.

---

- **全体（ぜんたい）** — whole, entirety, total; noun. Used to refer to the sum total or overall picture. 全体で means "in total, altogether." [JLPT N3]
- **従業員（じゅうぎょういん）** — employee(s). [JLPT N3]
- **ぐらい** — about, approximately. [JLPT N5]

I plan to rewrite the last part of the report.

---

- **部分（ぶぶん）** — part, portion, section; noun. Shared with Chinese (部分 bùfen), same meaning. Contrast: 全体 (whole). [JLPT N3]
- **〜つもりだ** — "intend to, plan to." Expresses the speaker's intention. [JLPT N4]
- **書き直す（かきなおす）** — to rewrite. 書く + 直す(なおす) "to do again, redo." [JLPT N3]

The EU unified its currency to the euro.

---

- **統一する（とういつ）** — to unify, standardize, integrate; transitive verb. Bringing multiple things into one consistent system. 通貨をユーロに統一する = unified the currency to the euro. [JLPT N2]
- **通貨（つうか）** — currency. [JLPT N2]
- **〜に統一する** — note the particle に indicates the target state (unified to/into X).

The map was small and hard to read, so I made an enlarged copy.

---

- **拡大する（かくだい）** — to enlarge, expand, magnify; transitive verb. Used for enlarging images, expanding scope/scale. Contrast: 縮小する (to reduce). [JLPT N2]
- **拡大コピー** — enlarged copy (photocopy). Commonly used at convenience stores and copy shops. [JLPT N2]
- **小さくて** — te-form of the i-adjective 小さい, used to give a reason: "because it is small..." [JLPT N5]
- **見づらい（みにづらい）** — hard to see/read. 〜づらい indicates difficulty in doing something. 見にくい(みにくい) is also possible with nearly the same meaning. [JLPT N3]

I reduced a B4 page to A4 size and copied it.

---

- **縮小する（しゅくしょう）** — to reduce, shrink, scale down; transitive verb. Used for reducing size, scale, or scope. Contrast: 拡大する (to enlarge). [JLPT N2]
- **B4をA4に** — note the particle に marks the target size/state after reduction. [JLPT N5]

"Those taking the interview, please gather at the venue 30 minutes before the scheduled time."

---

- **集合する（しゅうごう）** — to gather, assemble, meet up; intransitive verb. Used for people gathering at a designated place/time. 集合時間(しゅうごうじかん) = meeting time. [JLPT N2]
- **会場（かいじょう）** — venue, meeting place. [JLPT N3]
- **〜てください** — imperative request form. [JLPT N5]

The river flows from northeast to southwest.

---

- **方向（ほうこう）** — direction, orientation; noun. Shared with Chinese (方向 fāngxiàng), same meaning. 方向に流れる = flows in the direction of. [JLPT N3]
- **北東（ほくとう）** — northeast. 南西(なんせい) = southwest. [JLPT N2]
- **流れる（ながれる）** — to flow; intransitive verb. Used for rivers, time, blood, etc. [JLPT N4]

We arranged the desks with 50-centimeter gaps between them.

---

- **間隔（かんかく）** — interval, gap, space (between objects or events); noun. Note: the reading is かんかく, not んかく (the source text appears to have a typo). Refers to physical distance or time intervals. [JLPT N2]
- **間隔をあける** — set phrase: to leave/keep a gap or interval. あける is transitive (to open/make space). [JLPT N3]
- **並べる（ならべる）** — to line up, arrange (in a row); transitive verb. Intransitive counterpart: 並ぶ(ならぶ). [JLPT N4]

Place the thermometer under the armpit to take the temperature.

---

- **脇（わき）** — armpit; side, flank; noun. A wago term. The primary meaning is "armpit" but it also means "side" (道の脇 "the side of the road") and "besides, apart from" (脇に置く "set aside"). [JLPT N2]
- **わきの下（した）** — under the armpit. [JLPT N4]
- **はさんで** — te-form of 挟む(はさむ) "to hold between, clamp." 体温計を挟む = hold the thermometer between (the body and arm). [JLPT N3]
- **測る（はかる）** — to measure (temperature, weight, etc.). For time, use 計る; for area/volume, 測る or 計る. [JLPT N4]

Cross the border by car.

---

- **通過する（つうか）** — to pass through, go through (a place, point, stage); intransitive verb. Used for physical passage (国境を通過する) and abstract passage (試験を通過する "pass an exam stage"). Takes を for the place passed through. [JLPT N2]
- **国境（こっきょう）** — border (between countries). Note: the kun-yomi くにざかい also exists but is rare. [JLPT N2]

On this trip, all transportation will be by bus.

---

- **移動する（いどう）** — to move, relocate, travel (from one place to another); intransitive/transitive verb. Refers to changing location. As a noun, 移動 means "travel, movement, relocation." [JLPT N2]
- **旅行（りょこう）** — trip, travel. [JLPT N4]
- **すべて** — all, entirely. Here it modifies 移動: "all travel/movement." [JLPT N4]

Due to a power outage, that supermarket suspended operations.

---

- **停止する（ていし）** — to stop, suspend, halt (operations, functions); transitive/intransitive verb. Used for machines, services, operations. 営業を停止する = suspend business operations. [JLPT N2]
- **停電（ていでん）** — power outage, blackout. [JLPT N2]
- **ため** — because of, due to. Formal reason marker. [JLPT N3]

The higher you climb, the more the temperature drops.

---

- **低下する（ていか）** — to decline, drop, deteriorate; intransitive verb. Used for temperature, ability, quality, performance, etc. Contrast: 向上(こうじょう)する (to improve). [JLPT N2]
- **〜ば〜ほど** — "the more... the more..." conditional correlative construction. 登れば登るほど = "the more you climb, the more..." [JLPT N3]
- **気温（きおん）** — air temperature. [JLPT N3]

Her luggage exceeded the weight limit by 10 kilos.

---

- **超過する（ちょうか）** — to exceed, go over (a limit, standard); transitive verb. Takes を to mark what is exceeded. 規定の重量を超過する = exceed the weight limit. [JLPT N2]
- **規定（きてい）** — regulation, rule, standard. [JLPT N2]
- **重量（じゅうりょう）** — weight (of an object, cargo). Kango; wago equivalent would be 重さ(おもさ). [JLPT N2]
- **〜も** — emphatic particle: "as much as, no less than." Emphasizes the surprisingly large amount. [JLPT N4]

Stand up from a chair.

---

- **立ち上がる（たちあがる）** — to stand up, get up; intransitive verb. Literal physical meaning. Also used figuratively: 立ち上がる = "to get back on one's feet" after a setback, or "to launch/start" (プロジェクトが立ち上がる). [JLPT N2]
- **いすから** — から marks the point of departure (from the chair). [JLPT N5]

Jump for joy.

---

- **飛び上がる（とびあがる）** — to jump up, leap into the air; intransitive verb. Literal: to jump up. Figurative: to be startled (驚いて飛び上がる), or to jump for joy (喜んで飛び上がる). [JLPT N2]
- **喜んで** — adverbial te-form of 喜ぶ(よろこぶ) "to be glad, rejoice." Describes the manner of jumping. [JLPT N4]

To surface, float up to the water's surface.

---

- **浮かび上がる（うかびあがる）** — to emerge, come to the surface, become visible; intransitive verb. Literal: to rise to the surface of water. Figurative: to come to light, become apparent (問題が浮かび上がる "a problem comes to light"), to stand out visually (像が浮かび上がる). [JLPT N2]
- **水面（すいめん）** — water surface. [JLPT N2]

{Sand/dust ...} swirls up into the air.

---

- **舞い上がる（まいあがる）** — to swirl up, flutter upward; intransitive verb. Evokes a light, swirling, dancing motion upward. Used for dust, sand, leaves, paper scraps. Figuratively: to be elated, get carried away with excitement (調子に舞い上がる). [JLPT N2]
- **砂（すな）** — sand. ほこり = dust. [JLPT N3]

{Fire/fighting spirit/love ...} blazes up, burns fiercely.

---

- **燃え上がる（もえあがる）** — to blaze up, burn intensely; intransitive verb. The 上がる intensifies the burning action to completion/climax. Used literally for fire and figuratively for emotions (闘志 "fighting spirit," 恋心 "love"). [JLPT N2]
- **闘志（とうし）** — fighting spirit, competitive drive. [JLPT N1]
- **恋心（こいごころ）** — feelings of love, romantic feelings. A wago compound. [JLPT N1]

The muscles are bulging/swollen.

---

- **盛り上がる（もりあがる）** — to bulge, swell, rise up; to become excited/lively; intransitive verb. Literal: to bulge or rise up (muscles, ground swelling). Figurative: to get excited, lively, heated (パーティーが盛り上がる). The example sentence shows the literal/physical meaning. [JLPT N2]
- **筋肉（きんにく）** — muscle. [JLPT N2]
- Note: This word is very commonly used in the figurative sense (パーティーが盛り上がる "the party gets lively").

Cheers erupt/rise up.

---

- **沸き上がる/湧き上がる（わきあがる）** — to well up, surge forth, erupt; intransitive verb. The kanji 沸 is used for boiling/voices; 湧 is used for water springing up. Used for emotions, cheers, enthusiasm surging up spontaneously. 歓声が沸き上がる is a fixed collocation. [JLPT N2]
- **歓声（かんせい）** — cheers, shouts of joy. [JLPT N2]

A clear, cloudless autumn sky.

---

- **晴れ上がる（はれあがる）** — to clear up completely, become cloudless; intransitive verb. The 上がる emphasizes complete clearing — not just "clearing a bit" but fully clear skies. Often used as a modifier: 晴れ上がった空. [JLPT N2]
- **秋空（あきぞら）** — autumn sky. A poetic/seasonal compound (季語). [JLPT N2]

To tremble/shiver with {cold/fear ...}.

---

- **震え上がる（ふるえあがる）** — to tremble violently, shake with fear/cold; intransitive verb. The 上がる intensifies the trembling to an extreme degree. Takes に for the cause (寒さに震え上がる). [JLPT N2]
- **恐怖（きょうふ）** — fear, terror. A compound of two near-synonyms (恐れる + 怖い), typical of kango formation. [JLPT N2]

To cower, shrink with {cold/fear ...}.

---

- **縮み上がる（ちぢみあがる）** — to shrink, cower, huddle up (from cold or fear); intransitive verb. Similar to 震え上がる but emphasizes the physical act of making oneself small/cowering rather than shaking. Takes に for the cause. [JLPT N2]
- Note: 縮み上がる and 震え上がる share the same pattern (〜に縮み上がる/震え上がる) but differ in the physical response — shrinking vs. trembling.

{A pond/lake/river ...} dries up.

---

- **干上がる（ひあがる）** — to dry up, run dry; intransitive verb. Used for bodies of water drying completely. The 上がる indicates completion. [JLPT N2]
- **池（いけ）** — pond. 湖(みずうみ) = lake. 川(かわ) = river. [JLPT N4]

The food/meal is ready.

---

- **でき上がる（できあがる）** — to be completed, finished, ready; intransitive verb. The 上がる adds the nuance of thorough completion. Commonly used for meals, products, buildings. Essentially synonymous with できる but emphasizes the completed state more strongly. [JLPT N2]
- **料理（りょうり）** — cooking, dish, meal. [JLPT N4]

Lift up a load/baggage.

---

- **持ち上げる（もちあげる）** — to lift, raise (physically); transitive verb. Literal meaning. Also used figuratively: to flatter, praise excessively (お世辞で持ち上げる), or to push up (prices). [JLPT N2]
- **荷物（にもつ）** — luggage, baggage, load. [JLPT N3]

Look up at the sky.

---

- **見上げる（みあげる）** — to look up at; transitive verb. The 上げる indicates the upward direction of gaze. Literal: to look up at something above (空を見上げる). Figurative: to look up to, respect (尊敬する sense: 親を見上げる), or to be impressive/daunting. [JLPT N2]

Stack up documents/materials.

---

- **積み上げる（つみあげる）** — to pile up, stack; to accumulate; transitive verb. Literal: to pile things up high. Figurative: to accumulate achievements, experience, evidence (実績を積み上げる). The 上がる emphasizes piling to a significant height. [JLPT N2]
- **資料（しりょう）** — materials, data, documents. [JLPT N3]

Launch {a rocket/fireworks}.

---

- **打ち上げる（うちあげる）** — to launch, fire (a rocket, fireworks); to finish up, wrap up; transitive verb. Literal: to shoot/launch something upward. Also means "to conclude, wrap up" (会議を打ち上げる) — the image is of something being "thrown up" as a finale. [JLPT N2]
- **ロケット** — rocket (loanword). 花火(はなび) = fireworks. [JLPT N3]

Start up a computer.

---

- **立ち上げる（たちあげる）** — to start up, launch (a computer, program, project); transitive verb. In modern usage, this is the standard term for booting a computer (PCを立ち上げる) or launching a new project/business. The image is of something "standing up" from a stopped state. Distinguished from 立ち上がる (intransitive, entry 371). [JLPT N2]
- **コンピューター** — computer (loanword). Often abbreviated as PC or パソコン. [JLPT N4]

Let's wrap up work at 5 o'clock today.

---

- **切り上げる（きりあげる）** — to wrap up, bring to a close; to round up (a number); transitive verb. The image is of "cutting off" and moving to the next thing. Used for ending work, conversations, etc. (仕事を切り上げる). In mathematics: to round up (a number). Contrast: 切り下げる(きりさげる) = to round down. [JLPT N2]
- **〜で** — particle marking the time/point at which the action stops: "at 5 o'clock." [JLPT N5]
